rules.title: Start important actions yourself
rules.guidance: If a message or link asks you to sign in, pay, confirm identity or enter sensitive data, do not continue from the supplied link. Open the official app or site yourself.

rules.title: Verify the payment recipient
rules.guidance: Before paying, verify the recipient, amount and purpose. Treat unexpected changes to bank details or payment instructions as a reason to verify independently.

rules.title: Urgency means pause
rules.guidance: Pressure, threats and “act now” language are common social-engineering tools. Slow down before doing anything consequential.

rules.title: Verify unusual requests another way
rules.guidance: If a colleague, bank, manager, friend or relative unexpectedly asks for money, codes or sensitive data, verify through a separate trusted channel.

rules.title: A message does not prove who sent it
rules.guidance: Names, logos, caller IDs, email addresses and profile images can be spoofed or copied. Verify identity independently when the request matters.

rules.title: When in doubt, verify first
rules.guidance: Uncertainty is a reason to stop and check, not a reason to take a risk.

rules.title: Never share passwords, PINs or verification codes
rules.guidance: Do not send, dictate or enter passwords, PINs or one-time verification codes because another person tells you to.

rules.title: Use a unique password for every account
rules.guidance: Password reuse lets one breach threaten many accounts.

rules.title: Use a long passphrase or generated password
rules.guidance: Prefer long, unique and unpredictable passwords. A password manager can generate them; if you must remember one, use a long passphrase not based on personal facts.

rules.title: Store passwords safely
rules.guidance: Use a password manager instead of unprotected notes, documents, email drafts or contact fields.

rules.title: Use passkeys or multi-factor authentication
rules.guidance: Use a passkey or other phishing-resistant method where available. Otherwise enable multi-factor or two-step verification.

rules.title: Protect your primary email account
rules.guidance: Your primary email is often the recovery path for other accounts. Give it stronger authentication and secure recovery settings.

rules.title: Review important account security settings
rules.guidance: Periodically review sign-in methods, recovery information, active sessions and security notifications.

rules.title: Remove old devices and unnecessary access
rules.guidance: Revoke sessions, devices and connected applications you no longer use or recognize.

rules.title: Lock phones and computers
rules.guidance: Use a strong device PIN/password or biometrics and enable automatic locking.

rules.title: Keep devices and software updated
rules.guidance: Install security updates promptly and enable automatic updates where practical.

rules.title: Keep built-in protection enabled
rules.guidance: Keep supported anti-malware, firewall and platform security protections enabled and current. Install mobile apps from trusted official stores.

rules.title: Secure home Wi-Fi and the router
rules.guidance: Change default administrator credentials, keep router firmware current, use modern Wi-Fi security such as WPA3 where supported, and disable unnecessary remote administration.

rules.title: Make backups you can restore
rules.guidance: Keep important data in separate backups and periodically test that recovery actually works.

rules.title: Consider protective DNS or equivalent network filtering
rules.guidance: A reputable protective DNS or equivalent network-level service can block access to known malicious domains. Treat it as an additional control, not a guarantee.

rules.title: Treat unexpected attachments and QR codes with caution
rules.guidance: Unexpected attachments, links and QR codes can lead to malware or phishing. Verify the sender and context before opening them.

rules.title: Do not install remote-access software because a stranger tells you to
rules.guidance: Scammers may ask you to install remote-control or “security” software. Do not hand control of your device to an unsolicited caller or message sender.

rules.title: Polished design is not proof of trust
rules.guidance: A fraudulent website, profile or advertisement can look professional. Verify the domain, source and whether you initiated the action.

rules.title: Be cautious with too-good-to-be-true offers and emotional stories
rules.guidance: Scams often use extraordinary investment returns, inheritance stories, romance or emergencies to create trust and pressure before asking for money or data.

rules.title: Report and respond quickly
rules.guidance: Stop the activity, preserve relevant evidence, secure affected accounts and contact the relevant service provider or financial institution. Report the incident to the appropriate national cyber authority or law-enforcement channel where applicable.
